Quick start — from a fresh install to your first backup

Step by step from a newly installed SATOM to a registered, discovered appliance with its first configuration backup in the vault.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view appliances.edit appliances.apply backups.view backups.create users.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → Appliances (URL /appliances) · FortiWeb ADOM → Operations → Device Backups
On this page
  • Before you start
  • Step 1 — Sign in and secure the admin account
  • Step 2 — Create personal accounts
  • Step 3 — Register the appliance
  • Step 4 — Test the connection

  • Step 6 — Take the first backup

  • If something fails
  • "Name and host are required."

Before you start#

You need:

  • SATOM installed and reachable over HTTPS (see Installation). The installer asks for the admin password; the guided setup can generate one into a root-only file on the server.
  • One appliance — FortiWeb is used in this guide — with its management address, HTTPS port and an API-capable administrator account on the appliance.
  • Network access from the SATOM server to the appliance's management port (and SSH, if you want SSH-based backups or CLI capture).
  1. 1Sign in as adminChange the installation password
  2. 2Create your own accountsOne person, one account
  3. 3Register the applianceAppliances → Add Appliance
  4. 4Test the connectionAppliance page → Test Connection
  5. 5Discover itDiscovery → Start discovery
  6. 6Take the first backupDevice Backups → Create Backup
  7. 7ConfirmBell notification, Jobs page, backup listed in the vault

Step 1 — Sign in and secure the admin account#

  1. Browse to your SATOM address, for example https://satom.example.com.
  2. Sign in as admin with the installation password. You land on the Global home, which says No appliances registered yet.
  3. Open the user menu (top right) → Profile → Change Password, set a new password (12 to 1024 characters) and click Update Password.
  4. Optional but recommended: on the same page click Set up 2FA.

See First login for details.

Step 2 — Create personal accounts#

Open Global → Administrator → Users and create one account per person, choosing a profile (readonly, operator or admin). Directory users can sign in once an administrator has configured Settings → Authentication. See Users and profiles.

Step 3 — Register the appliance#

  1. In the Global ADOM open Administrator → Appliances in the sidebar. (A profile without the administrator capability finds it under Global → Appliances, or Operations → Appliances inside a product ADOM. Inside a product ADOM the page only accepts that product.)
  2. Click Add Appliance.
  3. Fill in the form:
Field Description Required Example
Name Unique name shown everywhere in SATOM. Yes fweb-01
Kind The product. Yes FortiWeb
Host / IP Management address. Yes 192.0.2.10
Port Management HTTPS port. Yes (default 443) 443
Username / Password Appliance administrator used by SATOM. The password is stored encrypted. Yes satom-api
VDOM (optional) The appliance-side ADOM when the FortiWeb runs in ADOM mode. No root
Tags (comma-separated) Free labels. No prod, eu
Zone, Line, Department Classification (lists maintained by an administrator). No dmz
Verify SSL certificate Validate the appliance's HTTPS certificate. Needs the issuing CA in the trust store for a private CA. No ticked
Maintenance mode Hide the appliance from operators. Shown only to users who may see maintenance devices. No —
This is an HA cluster (node 0) Register an HA pair as one logical cluster; add member nodes afterwards. No —
  1. Click Add Appliance. The page confirms "Appliance fweb-01 created." — possibly followed by the metrics collectors and threshold probes that were provisioned for it — and opens the appliance page.

🔑Permission

Opening the Appliances list and an appliance page needs appliances.view — the sidebar entry is shown to the same users; creating an appliance needs write access (for example appliances.edit). Operators therefore register appliances from the menu; no administrator capability is needed.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the Appliances list, the appliance page and Test Connection require View appliances (appliances.view), and the Appliances entry moved from the Administrator group to the Global / Fleet group of the sidebar.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: Appliances is back under Administrator for administrators; every other profile with appliances.view keeps it in the Global / Fleet group.

Step 4 — Test the connection#

On the appliance page click Test Connection. It shows Connection OK, or Connection failed: . Fix the address, port, credentials or certificate setting with Edit until it succeeds.

Step 5 — Discover the appliance#

  1. On the appliance page click Discovery (it is called Rediscovery once a first snapshot exists).
  2. Optionally tick Capture full WPP + policy depth (slow) and Also capture the CLI configuration (SSH, slow).
  3. Click Start discovery and watch Progress. Stop ends the sweep after the current read; nothing is written and the previous snapshot is kept.

Discovery is read-only: it fills SATOM's own copy of the configuration so the policy and object pages can render. It needs appliances.apply. See Rediscovery.

Step 6 — Take the first backup#

  1. Enter the FortiWeb ADOM (Global sidebar → ADOMs → FortiWeb).
  2. Make sure the appliance is selected in the top bar (click the device area → Switch device to pick it).
  3. Open Operations → Device Backups. The backup vault of the appliance opens. (From any appliance page, View Backups opens the same vault.)
  4. Choose the capture method — Auto (REST → SSH) is the default — and click Create Backup (on an empty vault: Create First Backup).
  5. The page says "Backup started for fweb-01 — you'll be notified when it completes (track it in the Jobs dock)."

🔑Permission

Opening the vault (and the Device Backups entry) needs backups.view. Creating backups needs backups.create (or backups.restore); Download needs backups.create. Buttons you cannot use are hidden.

Step 7 — Confirm it worked#

  • The bell shows Backup ready: fweb-01; clicking it opens the vault.
  • The vault lists the new backup with its date, size, source (Device), firmware and who took it. Download saves the .conf file.
  • The Jobs page shows the finished Backup — fweb-01 job.
  • The Global home FortiWeb card now counts 1 appliance.

If something fails#

"Name and host are required."#

Fill in Name and Host / IP (a VIP-mode cluster needs the shared VIP).

"Appliance name 'fweb-01' already exists."#

Names are unique; choose another one.

"This ADOM can only add FortiADC appliances."#

You are in a product ADOM; register the appliance from Global or from its own ADOM.

"Connection failed: …"#

Possible causes — wrong address or port, a firewall between SATOM and the appliance, wrong credentials, or Verify SSL certificate ticked for an appliance whose CA SATOM does not trust.

Solution — correct the entry with Edit, add the CA to the trust store or untick verification, then test again.

"Backup failed: fweb-01"#

The notification body explains the reason. If the appliance cannot produce a backup (for example a FortiWeb with a backup password set), use Upload .conf in the vault and store a file exported from the appliance. See Backups.

Next steps#

  • Schedule regular backups and syncs: Scheduled actions.
  • Explore the FortiWeb ADOM: Server policies.
  • File the appliance in your Bookmarks.
